application.outputs: The pallet pose (position and yaw of the pallet face in the camera RGB optical frame). The pallet width, height, and depth in metres. Which detected pallets are sent through stage 2 versus marked deferred. The handling process uses those results while the scene can still change, so the result must stay within the protected latency budget of 5 ms.
application.purpose: pps is the pallet perception stack on an AGV. It detects pallets in a scene that can still change and estimates a pose the vehicle can use for dynamic handling. Stage 1 is the RT-DETR detector, which publishes 2D pallet detections. Stage 2 is the chamfer geometry pipeline in geometry_core (estimate_pose_chamfer_v3_2), wrapped by pallet_pose_cpp_node: it synchronizes those detections with a depth image and estimates the pallet face pose in the camera RGB optical frame.
application.users: The vehicle's dynamic handling process. It needs a pallet pose while the scene can still change, so it can approach and handle the pallet. The rich PalletPoseStamped message is the pose result intended for that AGV controller.

kept_features.summary: For the class-matched detections in one capture, select_stage2_subset ranks that DetectionCandidate list with the strategy select_detection already implements. It applies that strategy by the first-maximum rule std::max_element already uses, so a tie keeps the earlier candidate and the later tied candidate stays deferred. It admits at most the count the caller passes, in that rank order, and places every candidate it does not admit into deferred, preserving their order in the candidate list. Each candidate keeps its source_index. Stage2Admission holds those two vectors, admitted and deferred. An empty candidate list returns both vectors empty, and an unknown strategy throws. The pose node calls it with its detection_selection strategy and a count of one, so stage 2 still estimates that single admitted pallet. The admitted source index and the deferred source indices are written on PalletPoseStamped after input_depth_stamp. The message already carries this pair's RGB and depth stamps, so the split is this capture while the scene can still change. When the estimate fails, publish no PalletPoseStamped and write the same two lists on the failure diagnostic, which is the only result that path publishes. The two early returns that publish nothing stay as they are. The user named which detections are sent through stage 2 versus marked deferred. The part they did not name is that the split is these two admission vectors, ordered by that first-maximum rule, on the pose result the handling process reads.

rejected_features.summary: Publish the pallet face width, height, and depth in metres on the stage-2 outcome and on PalletPoseStamped. Width and height are the spans of the plane inliers already built inside estimate_pose_chamfer_v3_2, along that estimate's plane axes. Depth is the mean z of those same inliers after the depth-to-RGB transform that already places the face centre. The handling process can then size the approach from this synchronized capture while the scene can still change.

For each stage-2 estimate, build the chamfer prototype from the width and height of the pallet face already recovered as plane inliers in that depth frame, instead of the fixed 1.20 m by 0.14 m factory face, so the template is the pallet the vehicle is about to handle.

For the detections in one capture, return which pallets are sent through stage 2 and which are deferred. select_stage2_subset ranks the existing DetectionCandidate list with the strategy select_detection already implements, admits at most the count this capture will pose, and places every remaining candidate in deferred. Stage2Admission holds those two vectors, admitted and deferred, and each candidate keeps its source_index. The pose node calls it with its detection_selection strategy and a count of one, so stage 2 still estimates that single admitted pallet, and the other candidates in this array stay on the deferred vector for this capture. An empty candidate list returns both vectors empty, and an unknown strategy throws. The count is set for this capture because the scene can still change and stage 2 poses a subset of the array.

For each synchronized detection and depth pair, send stage 2 the two class-matched pallet faces with the largest area_px, breaking remaining ties by higher score and then by lower source index, and mark every other candidate deferred. Each admitted face is passed to estimate_pose_chamfer_v3_2, and each success publishes its own PalletPoseStamped from that capture. Each deferred candidate is published as its source index together with this pair's RGB and depth stamps. A pair with fewer than two candidates admits every candidate and defers none. The handling process then has the poses of the large faces in this capture and the identities of the detections this pair did not pose, while the scene can still change.

For each successful call of estimate_pose_chamfer_v3_2, publish the pallet width, height, and depth in metres on the stage-2 outcome and on PalletPoseStamped. Width and height are the factory face that call already matches, params.pallet_width_m 1.20 m and params.pallet_height_m 0.14 m, and the search template stays that face. The face-centre position and yaw stay the pose. Depth is the length of this pallet along the face normal on the side farther from the camera, through the two fork openings the prototype already cuts. Of the points sample_face_points already returned, keep those that, after the plane projection is translated by the opposite of best_pose's tx and ty and rotated by the opposite of the rotation rotate_proto_into applies, fall inside either pocket rectangle: centres at plus and minus pocket_centre_offset_m along the prototype width axis, with sides pocket_width_m and pocket_height_m. A point counts only when its signed point_to_plane_distance is less than the negation of plane_inlier_threshold_m. The camera-facing normal makes that negative side the side farther from the camera, and the point's contribution is the negation of that signed distance. depth_m is the median of those contributions. has_body_depth is true only when that set is non-empty. When the set is empty, has_body_depth is false, publish_pose still publishes the pose with the factory face width and height, and the handling process reads depth_m as a body length only when has_body_depth is true. The fields width_m, height_m, depth_m, and has_body_depth are written on the outcome and, after input_depth_stamp, on PalletPoseStamped. A failed estimate still publishes no PalletPoseStamped. The two early returns in on_pair stay silent. Stage 2 still runs once, on the one candidate select_detection already chooses. The rich message already carries this pair's RGB and depth stamps, so the sizes belong to this capture while the scene can still change. The user named the three sizes. The part they did not name is that depth is the median far-side length through those two pocket openings, and that has_body_depth is false when the openings show no body.
